scope: The public LangGraph v1.x concept surface as documented upstream, with per-concept mini-ork YAML equivalents (or explicit divergent-by-design lines) — the auditor pass for the 20261012-langgraph-parity-survey family; siblings cover lens-D2 (stategraph construction), lens-D3 (persistence / checkpointers), and lens-D4 (streaming modes).
citation_convention: Every concept's claim line carries at least one inline citation — either a URL to a verifiable LangGraph source or a relative path into the mini-ork tree. The citation sits on the same physical line as the claim (D1 hard rule C4), so a grep on the claim line returns a citation.
yaml_convention: Every concept ends with either a fenced YAML block showing the smallest faithful mini-ork equivalent, OR a single line beginning with `divergent-by-design:` with a one-line rationale (D1 hard rule F4).

claims.semantics_summary: A typed, directed graph of nodes and edges whose edges carry a State schema. The runtime walks the graph node-by-node, merging each node's return dict into the running state and routing the next node by the declared edge set. The state schema is a TypedDict (or Pydantic / dataclass); the runtime rejects writes that don't conform. Conditional edges and Command returns re-enter the routing table.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Closes the central parity claim — every other LangGraph concept in this report hangs off this one, so making 'graph = workflow.yaml' true is the chapter's anchor.
claims.value_any_task: Any recipe needs a typed graph with deterministic edge routing; the declared-edges vocabulary is what every other node-type enum nests into.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep `recipes/<name>/workflow.yaml` as the smallest faithful analog; the closed `edge_type` enum in `schemas/workflow.schema.json` already mirrors the routing surface D1 needs.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x passes a typed State object through every node; each node reads the channels it needs and returns a partial dict that the runtime operator.add / operator.or_-merges into the running state, with one optional Annotated[..., reducer] reducer per channel. mini-ork carries the same shape via task_class.yaml + per-node outputs:, but merge is not first-class — there is no `merge:` enum on the output schema.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The chapter epic must choose whether to (a) declare a merge enum on the artifact contract or (b) continue routing reductions through downstream transform nodes; D1 framed that choice but didn't resolve it.
claims.value_any_task: Any recipe whose nodes return overlapping keys hits the same merge question; resolving the chapter decision gives every downstream recipe a free answer.
claims.proposed_shape: First-class `merge:` enum on `schemas/artifact_contract.schema.json` (or keep transform-node routing) — the open question D1 flagged.

claims.semantics_summary: A langgraph node is a callable (sync or async) that receives the current state and a RunnableConfig, and returns either a partial state dict or a Command that combines a state update with a routing decision. mini-ork's nodes: array is the declarative equivalent: each node has a type from the closed enum (planner, researcher, transform, implementer, reviewer, verifier, eval, reflector, publisher, rollback), a prompt_ref, an optional model_lane, a dispatch_mode from serial|parallel|partitioned|speculative, an optional retry: block, an optional gates: list, an optional mcp_servers: list, an optional tools: array, and a typed inputs/outputs port block. The RunnableConfig analog is RunContext (mini_ork.context.RunContext, mini_ork/context.py:59).
claims.value_chapter_epic: The node-type enum is the chapter's central vocabulary; every other parity claim (Command, START/END, Send, interrupts, tool calls, structured output) is a property of one or more node rows, so the chapter's faithfulness rides on this enum remaining closed and accurate.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe declares nodes; making sure the schema-richness of a `stateful callable` is captured recipe-declaratively is a per-task requirement.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep `WorkflowNode` (`schemas/workflow.schema.json`) as the smallest faithful analog; closed enum already names every concept D1 calls out.

claims.semantics_summary: A langgraph edge is a static or conditional link from one node to the next; the edge set forms the routing table the runtime consults after each node returns. mini-ork's edges: array is the same shape: each edge has from, to, and an edge_type from the closed enum (depends_on, supplies_context_to, verifies, blocks, retries, escalates_to, human_decision_gate, verifies_user_choice). Finer-grained branching lives in the optional `condition:` object on retries edges (a jsonschema-backed predicate registered at compile time — the F5/F6 contract from `p1-1-condition-edges`).
claims.value_chapter_epic: Edges carry the same declarative routing surface the chapter needs; closing the F5/F6 contract (condition-only-on-retries + policy-registry-for-run-level) is part of what the chapter claims.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe's routing decisions are encoded in edges; making sure the enum covers every graph routing primitive is a hard pre-condition for parity.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep `WorkflowEdge` (per `schemas/workflow.schema.json`) plus the `condition:` block (P1.1) consumed only on retries edges today; the policy registry stays for run-level routing, not per-edge branching.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph conditional edges attach a Python callable to an edge; the runtime evaluates the callable against the post-node state and routes to the named branch. mini-ork's P1.1 conditional edges carry a typed `condition:` object instead — a jsonschema predicate with a pointer (RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the source node's output artifact JSON) and a match schema fragment; the runtime uses jsonschema Draft7 validator to decide whether the branch fires. The condition: block is consumed only on `retries` edges today — every other edge type is gated by the rc channel.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Resolving whether condition: stays retries-only (the current P1.1 contract) or widens to other edge types is an open chapter question the survey frames but does not close.
claims.value_any_task: Conditional branching is a common need; deciding whether the runtime commits to a jsonschema-only predicate (vs. allowing arbitrary functions) shapes every downstream recipe.
claims.proposed_shape: Maintain `condition:` as a jsonschema-backed pointer/match; document the open question whether to widen beyond retries edges as the chapter epic's explicit pending decision.

claims.semantics_summary: A langgraph Command is a single return value that combines a partial state update with a goto: routing decision, so a node can both write state and pick the next node in one step. mini-ork does not have an atomic write+route primitive in the same sense: a node's declared outputs are materialized after verifier gates pass, and the routing decision lives on the downstream edges entry (typically a retries edge with a condition: predicate). The split is declarative — there is no literal Command return.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The chapter's stated divergence (no single-return write+pick-next primitive) is honest and the closest analog (outputs: + retries-with-condition:) is well-documented — that's worth preserving in the chapter epic.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need write-and-route atomicity already route through retries-condition pairs; the documented divergence keeps call sites clear.
claims.proposed_shape: Divergent-by-design: keep the two-row pattern (`outputs:` plus `edges:` with `condition:`); no Command analog introduced.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph reserves the node names START (a virtual source node) and END (a virtual sink) to anchor the entry and exit of every graph; the runtime injects them when the graph is compiled. mini-ork has the same anchor concept: every recipe's nodes: array has an implicit entry node chosen by the task_class declared on the workflow header, and a rollback_strategy: field that names the terminal-failure node. There is no literal START/END row in the recipe — the executor resolves them at dispatch time; the audit log records the resolved entry and terminal node.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Implicit entry + rollback-strategy naming already mirror START/END; the chapter can cite this as parity-true without further work.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe needs an entry and a terminal; documenting the audit-log surface (which D1 does) avoids reinventing START/END per recipe.
claims.proposed_shape: No literal row; resolved at dispatch from task_class and rollback_strategy, with audit-log emission already wired.

claims.semantics_summary: A langgraph checkpointer is a pluggable backend (Memory, SQLite, Postgres) that records a Checkpoint after every superstep, keyed by (thread_id, checkpoint_id, checkpoint_ns), so a run can be replayed, time-travelled, or forked from any prior checkpoint. mini-ork's persistence story lives in two places, neither a direct analog: the artifact filesystem under ${MINI_ORK_RUN_DIR}/ plus the single-writer lease registered through mini_ork/stores/lease.py, and the in-process RunContext (mini_ork/context.py:59). There is no env-var knob named MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND and no MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK one-shot CLI override — neither string exists in mini_ork/.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The chapter epic must decide whether to introduce MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK as a v2 surface or keep documenting divergent-by-design — D1 frames this as the persistence chapter's central question.
claims.value_any_task: Run-level recovery is genuinely needed for long-running recipes; the divergence is real and the chapter owns it.
claims.proposed_shape: Either (a) introduce MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK as a new persistence module, or (b) document the divergence as a permanent reminder that recovery is via the `recursion:` block.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph keys every checkpoint with a thread_id (a logical session) and a checkpoint_id (a monotonic per-thread counter), and exposes both on the RunnableConfig so a node can read its own position. mini-ork's RunContext exposes run_id (stable for the run, the closest analog of thread_id), but there is no attempt_sha attribute on RunContext and no `<output>.attempt-<sha>.json` sidecar file produced by the dispatcher. A grep across mini_ork/ returns no attempt_sha symbol and no attempt-<sha> path literal.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Adding attempt_sha + the attempt-<sha> sidecar is the natural extension of any future persistence story; the chapter epic should at least spell out whether the missing surface is a planned gap or a permanent one.
claims.value_any_task: Per-output attempt sha is useful for debuggability; deciding whether to add it costs almost nothing once MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND is on the table.
claims.proposed_shape: Add `attempt_sha` to `RunContext` and write `<output>.attempt-<sha>.json` sidecars from the dispatcher.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x splits memory into short-term (in-thread State that dies with the run) and long-term (a Store that survives across threads and is keyed by namespace + key). mini-ork has a partial mirror: the artifact filesystem under ${MINI_ORK_RUN_DIR}/ is the short-term memory, and the semantic-memory layer in mini_ork/memory/semantic.py is the long-term store (addressable by {namespace, key, embedder}). The store is pluggable: register an embedder via mini_ork.memory.semantic.register_embedder_provider(name, factory) (mini_ork/memory/semantic.py:178) and select it at dispatch time with MO_EMBED_PROVIDER. There is no MO_MEMORY_STORE env var in the source tree.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The long-term store sits at semantic-memory today; the chapter should keep framing it as the long-term persistence layer (since §8 persistence is divergent-by-design).
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that benefit from a namespace-keyed store have it via the embedder provider registry already; MO_EMBED_PROVIDER is the knob.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep the in-tree semantic layer + MO_EMBED_PROVIDER; document the absence of MO_MEMORY_STORE as an explicit divergence.

claims.semantics_summary: A langgraph subgraph is a StateGraph composed as a node inside a parent graph; the runtime treats the subgraph as a single node from the parent's point of view, with its own internal state schema and routing. mini-ork's compositional unit is a recipe (a workflow.yaml + artifact_contract.yaml + task_class.yaml directory under recipes/), but there is no first-class sub-recipe-as-node feature in the WorkflowNode.type enum declared by schemas/workflow.schema.json — that enum is closed and has no subrecipe entry, no recipe_ref field on the WorkflowNode schema.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Sub-recipe composition is the chapter's largest compositional gap; the recursion block on the workflow header handles self-recursion but not child-recipe composition — the chapter epic should frame whether to introduce `type: subrecipe`.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes composed of sub-recipes today route through recursion; once sub-recipe node is a thing, the chapter closes a real workflow authoring pain point.
claims.proposed_shape: Introduce `type: subrecipe` plus `recipe_ref: ...` on `WorkflowNode` to enable first-class child-recipe composition.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph's Send is a per-input routing primitive that lets a node fan out one sub-invocation per element of an input list, and the runtime collects the partial states into a single reducer. mini-ork's dispatch_mode: partitioned is the map primitive — a node declared partitioned is sharded by an item key declared on the node's partition_key field; the executor writes one attempt per partition. The reduce step is narrower than langgraph's — there is no in-recipe merge: enum on the output schema, so a recipe that needs list-reduction behavior either names a downstream transform node or relies on filesystem-level last-writer behavior.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Map is real (partitioned dispatch); reduce is the open chapter question — same direction as §2's merge enum question.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that fan out per-item already work via partitioned dispatch; the missing surface is the per-item reducer.
claims.proposed_shape: Same answer as §2: first-class `merge:` enum on the output schema, or keep the transform-node routing pattern.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph executes independent branches of the DAG concurrently when the edge set exposes them; the runtime awaits the slowest branch before invoking the join node. mini-ork's parallel-execution story lives in the per-node dispatch_mode enum (serial|parallel|partitioned|speculative): a node declared parallel runs concurrently with its siblings in the same wave. There is no core-runtime MO_DISPATCH_WAVES knob, and the wave concept is implicit in the executor's readiness computation.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Parallel execution is parity-true today via dispatch_mode; the chapter can cite this as a present-side claim without further work.
claims.value_any_task: Any recipe that wants a wave-parallel default declares it on the workflow header; per-node opt-out uses dispatch_mode: serial.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep `dispatch_mode: parallel` on the workflow header and on individual nodes; no MO_DISPATCH_WAVES knob introduced.

claims.semantics_summary: A langgraph interrupt(...) call is a dynamic breakpoint that pauses the run and surfaces a payload to the caller; the caller can Command(resume=...) to inject a value and continue. mini-ork does not expose an in-process interrupt(...) callable. There is no type: human_in_the_loop node in the closed WorkflowNode.type enum. There is no finish_reason: "interrupt" value, no <run_dir>/.steering/<node>.json payload file, and no gate: human_review row. The closest analogs are (a) the human_decision_gate edge type — a static pre-publish halt, and (b) the operator-steering channel documented in docs/OPERATOR-STEERING.md.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Dynamic interrupts are the largest single chapter divergence — the in-process callable has no direct analog — so the chapter epic owns deciding whether to introduce the surface or keep the human_decision_gate + operator-steering workaround.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need mid-run injection use the operator-steering channel today; mid-node inject CLI is the existing workaround.
claims.proposed_shape: Either introduce `type: human_in_the_loop` plus `finish_reason: "interrupt"` plus a <run_dir>/.steering/<node>.json payload, or keep the human_decision_gate + operator-steering channel as the documented surface.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x unifies the human-in-the-loop surface under the interrupt / Command(resume=...) channel, plus a breakpoint parameter on .compile(...) for static pause points. mini-ork's human-in-the-loop surface is partial, and the two channels the report can cite are: (a) a human_decision_gate edge on the workflow, which halts the run before publishing, and (b) the operator-steering channel documented in docs/OPERATOR-STEERING.md. There is no type: human_in_the_loop node, no human_review_gate row, no <run_dir>/<run>/.steering/<node>.json payload.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Same direction as §14; the chapter's HITL decision (one surface or two) is the single source of truth.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that pause before publish do so today via human_decision_gate.
claims.proposed_shape: Consolidate the HITL decision with §14 — same answer applies.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph's durability contract is 'checkpoint before every external side effect, replay from the latest checkpoint on recovery, never duplicate a side effect.' mini-ork has a partial durability story today. The single-writer lease is real: mini_ork/stores/lease.py exposes is_lease_holder and refresh_lease, and a stale recovery refuses to publish over a newer one. The retry side is also real: mini_ork/workflow/retry.py writes <run_dir>/retry-exhausted/<node>.attempts.json. The effect-boundary half is narrower — there is no <run_dir>/.receipts/<tool>.json table, no per-tool receipt file.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Durability is the most-load-bearing chapter claim — the lack of an effect-boundary receipts table is the concrete divergence the chapter must own.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that call external tools use the single-writer lease today; per-tool receipts are the open gap.
claims.proposed_shape: Introduce `<run_dir>/.receipts/<tool>.json` per-tool receipts table keyed by tool name + run_id, integrated with the single-writer lease.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x ships five streaming modes: values, updates, events, debug, and custom (via get_stream_writer()). mini-ork's streaming surface is narrower. The only declared streaming primitive in the source tree is LiveWriter (defined at mini_ork/dispatch/live_stream.py:80, an append-only live-log writer with a byte-cap). There is no Stream envelope module at mini_ork.dispatch.stream, no StreamSink class, and no `mini-ork subscribe --run <run_id> --channel events --sink ws://...` CLI in the registered subcommands.
claims.value_chapter_epic: The five-channel stream surface is one of the chapter's largest divergences (alongside interrupts and persistence); the chapter epic owns whether to introduce a StreamSink class or continue with single-LiveWriter.
claims.value_any_task: The web UI consumes a tail of LiveWriter today; recipes that need a typed channel subscribe would need the StreamSink surface.
claims.proposed_shape: Introduce a StreamSink class + Stream envelope + per-channel subscribe CLI (`mini-ork subscribe --run <run_id> --channel events --sink ws://...`) in mini_ork/dispatch/stream.py.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x routes a model-emitted tool call to a registered ToolNode, which dispatches the call by name, returns the result, and lets the graph continue. mini-ork's tool surface is the tools: block on a node (per schemas/workflow.schema.json §WorkflowNode.tools) plus the parallel mcp_servers: list — both arrays of harness-tool names (or objects grouped by native / MCP capability) resolved against the tool registry. The dispatcher's mo_llm_dispatch wrapper (mini_ork.dispatch.llm_dispatch) and the ACP harness (mini_ork/acp_orchestrator/harness.py:113-140) pass the lists through --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --mcp-config, and --strict-mcp-config.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Tool calls are parity-true today — the schema covers both native tools and MCP servers; the chapter can mark this present without further work.
claims.value_any_task: Any recipe that needs a tool declares it on tools: or mcp_servers:; the harness handles the rest.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep `tools:` and `mcp_servers:` on WorkflowNode plus the structural invariant that no single node may simultaneously hold repo-write + untrusted-content ingress + outbound channel.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x binds a node's return to a pydantic.BaseModel (or TypedDict / dataclass) so the runtime can validate the schema and reject non-conforming writes. mini-ork's structured-output surface is the outputs: block on the artifact contract (per schemas/artifact_contract.schema.json) plus the per-node outputs: array on the workflow node (per schemas/workflow.schema.json §WorkflowNode.outputs). Each output declares a name, a path, and a kind — no mime: or merge: there. There is no materialize_outputs step in the source tree; the dispatcher does not currently emit finish_reason: "schema_violation" on a non-conforming artifact.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Structured output is parity-true at the schema layer; the chapter epic owns deciding whether to introduce a materialize_outputs step (or finish_reason: "schema_violation") to close the runtime-side gap.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need a fixed-shape output declare it on outputs:; the strict_handshake handshake is the closest parity surface today.
claims.proposed_shape: Add a `materialize_outputs` step in the dispatcher that emits `finish_reason: "schema_violation"` on a non-conforming artifact and tightens the strict_handshake description.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph's RetryPolicy is a NamedTuple of (initial_interval=0.5, backoff_factor=2.0, max_interval=128.0, max_attempts=3, jitter=True, retry_on=default_retry_on) and is attached to a node via add_node(..., retry=RetryPolicy(...)). mini-ork's P1.4 retry: block is the same five-field shape with the same defaults, sourced from the LangGraph named tuple (the source link LANGGRAPH_DEFAULTS_URL is defined at mini_ork/workflow/retry.py:56 and pins the upstream commit). The retryable-set is a closed enum over finish_reason values (timeout, infra_interrupt, provider_limit, network, overloaded, rate_limited, killed, sigterm, rc_137, rc_143 per mini_ork/recovery/auto_repair.py and mini_ork/learning/failure_classifier.py).
claims.value_chapter_epic: Retry policies are parity-true today — five-field same shape, defaults from upstream, retryable-set is a closed enum — the chapter can mark this present.
claims.value_any_task: Every recipe that needs retry declares it on the node; the closed enum and the attempt-log sidecar round out the parity story.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep the `retry:` block on WorkflowNode; keep `<run_dir>/retry-exhausted/<node>.attempts.json` as the attempt log.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x surfaces a RunnableConfig to every node with configurable, tags, metadata, and callbacks fields, and the graph compiles with with_config(...) / config_schema=.... mini-ork's RunContext is a partial analog: it carries the env contract from MINI_ORK_ROOT, MINI_ORK_HOME, MINI_ORK_DB, and MINI_ORK_RUN_DIR (defined at mini_ork/context.py:39-43), the run-identity vars (run_id), and the artifact manifest. There is no tags: block in the same sense as langgraph's configurable.tags, and no callbacks: field on RunContext. The risk_class: field on task_class.yaml is the closest analog of configurable.tags.
claims.value_chapter_epic: RunContext is a partial analog — env vars + run_id + manifest are real, tags/callbacks are not first-class; the chapter epic owns deciding whether to surface tags via risk_class or add a dedicated tags block.
claims.value_any_task: Run-level config lives in env vars today; recipes that need tags carry them via risk_class on task_class.
claims.proposed_shape: Either (a) document risk_class as the tags analog, or (b) add a `tags:` block to task_class.yaml.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x exposes a managed deployment surface (LangGraph Platform / Studio) that takes a compiled graph, runs it as a long-lived server, and serves a UI for tracing, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop. mini-ork's deployment surface is `mini-ork serve` (registered as a subcommand at mini_ork/cli/main.py:67, implemented in mini_ork/cli/serve.py, launched via bin/mini-ork-serve). There is no deploy/<recipe>.yaml per-recipe manifest, no mini-ork ui subcommand in the registered subcommand table, and no managed platform tier by design — the operator (self-hosted) tier is the recommended one.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Deployment is partial-parity by design — operator tier over managed platform; the chapter epic owns the framing 'same primitives, different surface' and not the gap.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that want long-lived execution run via `mini-ork serve` today; per-recipe deployment manifests are a documented absence.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep per-recipe packaging + operator tier; document the divergence so the chapter epic does not invent a managed-platform surface.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x integrates with MCP servers as tool providers: a graph declares an mcp_servers: list, and the runtime resolves the server list at compile time and exposes the tools to the LLM. mini-ork's MCP surface is the mcp_servers: list on a workflow node (see schemas/workflow.schema.json §WorkflowNode.mcp_servers), and the dispatcher passes the list through --mcp-config / --strict-mcp-config to the worker CLI (per mini_ork/acp_orchestrator/harness.py:135-140 and the --allowedTools construction in mini_ork/dispatch/providers.py:1403). The `mini-ork mcp add <name> --url <url> | --command <c>` CLI (mini_ork/cli/mcp_cmd.py:46) manages the project's MCP server list via mini_ork.dispatch.mcp_registry.
claims.value_chapter_epic: MCP is parity-true today — schema field + register CLI + harness flag plumbing — the chapter can mark this present.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that need an MCP server declare it on mcp_servers: so a reviewer can lint the capability grant.
claims.proposed_shape: Keep `mcp_servers:` on WorkflowNode; keep `mini-ork mcp add` CLI for register; harness keeps --mcp-config / --strict-mcp-config.

claims.semantics_summary: LangGraph v1.x supports replaying a thread from any prior checkpoint_id by passing thread_id + checkpoint_id to invoke / stream; the runtime loads the checkpoint, replays the graph from that point, and re-emits the events. mini-ork does not expose a time-travel CLI today. A grep across the registered subcommands returns no `mini-ork fork` command, no --run flag on a fork-shaped handler, and no --sha time-travel knob on any mini-ork invocation. The closest re-dispatch handle is the recipe-level recursion: block on the workflow header, which restarts a bounded control loop, not a per-attempt rewind.
claims.value_chapter_epic: Time travel is the natural follow-on of persistence; the chapter epic should not introduce it independently of §8/§9 — the same MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND decision gates it.
claims.value_any_task: Recipes that rewind use the recursion: block today; a per-attempt fork-shaped CLI is the planned gap.
claims.proposed_shape: Tie time travel to the §8 persistence decision — a fork-shaped `mini-ork fork --run --node --sha` CLI plus `<output>.attempt-<sha>.json` sidecars.

top_10_backlog.title: Persist + checkpoint: MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK + attempt_sha
top_10_backlog.rationale: §8 + §9 + §24 form the persistence/time-travel triangle; resolving any one of them gate-reveals the others and is the single largest parity gap in the chapter.

top_10_backlog.title: Interrupt channel: type: human_in_the_loop + finish_reason: interrupt + .steering/<node>.json payload
top_10_backlog.rationale: §14 + §15 share a single dynamic-interrupt surface; the chapter cannot claim HITL parity without it.

top_10_backlog.title: Streaming: StreamSink class + Stream envelope + per-channel subscribe CLI
top_10_backlog.rationale: §17 diverges from the five-channel langgraph surface; without a StreamSink the chapter cannot claim stream parity.

top_10_backlog.title: Sub-recipe node: type: subrecipe + recipe_ref on WorkflowNode
top_10_backlog.rationale: §11 closes the recipe-composition gap; without it the chapter cannot claim first-class sub-graph composition.

top_10_backlog.title: Per-tool effect-boundary receipts: <run_dir>/.receipts/<tool>.json
top_10_backlog.rationale: §16 durability's effect-boundary half is the concrete missing surface; introducing the receipts table is a one-module add.

top_10_backlog.title: Merge enum: first-class merge: field on the artifact contract output schema
top_10_backlog.rationale: §2 + §12 both hinge on the same merge question; a single merge: enum resolves both.

top_10_backlog.title: Conditional edges beyond retries: widen the condition: contract to other edge types
top_10_backlog.rationale: §5 documents that condition: is retries-only today; chapter needs to decide whether widening is worth the schema change.

top_10_backlog.title: Structured-output enforcement: materialize_outputs + finish_reason: schema_violation
top_10_backlog.rationale: §19 documents the runtime-side gap; tightening strict_handshake is the obvious next step.

top_10_backlog.title: RunConfig tags: surface configurable.tags as a dedicated tags block on task_class.yaml
top_10_backlog.rationale: §21 documents that risk_class is the current analog; deciding whether to introduce a dedicated tags block closes the partial analog.

top_10_backlog.title: Chapter synthesis: roll up the four lenses (auditor / stategraph / persistence / streaming) into a single chapter narrative
top_10_backlog.rationale: D1 + D2 (stategraph) + D3 (persistence / checkpointers) + D4 (streaming modes) form the four-lens chapter family; the synthesis is the public-facing document.

chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.title: Persistence chapter epic — three coupled decisions not yet made
chapter_epic_remaining_blockers.detail: MO_PERSISTENCE_BACKEND + MO_CHECKPOINT_FORK + attempt_sha + <output>.attempt-<sha>.json sidecar (D1 §8, §9, §24) are all parallel; resolving one without the others leaves the surface incoherent. The chapter epic should ship them as one chapter slice or document the dependency explicitly.
